mbm-1751.clue: The pastry under my bell never goes stale.
mbm-1751.quote: On canal rides my friend rings twice at every bridge with a bakery beyond it. I painted a little pastry under the bicycle bell. After fifty kilometers it starts to look freshly baked.

mbm-1752.clue: My shadow got a rainbow all to itself.
mbm-1752.quote: Under the open canopy I saw a small rainbow ring moving over the field. My instructor snapped a picture from beside me. It looks as if the sun put a gold button on my shadow.

mbm-1753.clue: Don't shake the book with the green ribbon.
mbm-1753.quote: I pressed a fern in my favorite adventure novel when I was twelve. At last summer's book swap a child opened to that page and asked if it had grown out of the jungle. I lent her the book.

mbm-1754.clue: We've been working on our handwriting at the gym.
mbm-1754.quote: My training partner and I sign the chalkboard after our sets, with arms still wobbling. The signatures are getting steadier. Mine started out looking like a badly drawn sheep. Now I add the tail on purpose.

mbm-1755.clue: My screen has a resident snail.
mbm-1755.quote: I wrote a download bar in the shape of a snail for Dad's old computer. When the file is ready the snail disappears into a flowerpot. Dad downloads things just to see it get home.

mbm-1756.clue: I play the hole that grew a tree.
mbm-1756.quote: Our shortest hole used to be straight. A little volunteer pine sprang up in the rough and grew into the line of sight over twenty years. I remember my first clear shot. My nephew has never seen one.

mbm-1757.clue: Our harbor is one book away from level.
mbm-1757.quote: The kitchen table slopes toward the window. We prop our board up on a book and keep spare pieces in an upside-down cup. Level is the moment both wooden boats stay in the harbor.

mbm-1758.clue: The audience didn't realize the rain was my job.
mbm-1758.quote: In our community theatre I tipped a box of dried peas for a rainstorm. Opening night my uncle asked how we'd got the roof to leak on cue. I let him take the thunder sheet home.

mbm-1759.clue: I save one tile in the shallow end just for waving.
mbm-1759.quote: When I touch the blue tile on my last lap my little brother waves through the pool window. Once he was late, so I swam a bonus lap. He thinks that's how you coach.

mbm-1760.clue: The pencil behind my ear is for drawing shoes.
mbm-1760.quote: At our alley you can tell the regulars by their bowling shoes. I sketch a pair beside each score. The day Dad rolled his first turkey he had little flames coming off both heels.

mbm-1761.clue: I owe a dance to the studio clock.
mbm-1761.quote: At our first lesson we couldn't hear the record over the wind. We waltzed to the clock ticks instead. For our anniversary I asked the teacher for three minutes with the music turned off.

mbm-1762.clue: I used the faded side on purpose.
mbm-1762.quote: I stitched sun-faded squares from our old picnic blanket beside the bright cloth from under its hem. My brother can point out where we used to set the lemonade jug.

mbm-1763.clue: I play a round with a goose egg in my pocket.
mbm-1763.quote: Granddad carved a little wooden egg for me after I went nine holes without keeping score. I carry it on the busy days when I'd rather count the clouds.

mbm-1764.quote: I hiked to see the waterfall and found it perfectly reflected in a pool at my feet. I drew all the upside-down trees first. A raindrop took the falls before I could finish.

mbm-1765.clue: My favorite opening uses the lid of a flask.
mbm-1765.quote: At the park we lost a white rook in a flowerbed. The lid of my thermos was just the right size. When I castled, three people at the next table raised their cups.

mbm-1766.clue: You can tell we've been dancing by the flour.
mbm-1766.quote: Mum and I worked out a ballroom turn in the bakery after closing. The next morning two spirals of shoe prints crossed the flour on the floor. We photographed them before sweeping.

mbm-1767.clue: I bring a little towel for the white squares.
mbm-1767.quote: Our park chess table catches the shade before anything else after a shower. I dried it square by square while my opponent moved the pieces onto the dry bit. We call that our rainy opening.

mbm-1768.clue: I've got a photograph with two horizons.
mbm-1768.quote: I took my first jump on a lake day so still the far shore had a perfect twin. Once the canopy opened I spent a whole minute looking for the seam between the skies.

mbm-1769.clue: I let the moth pick our bedtime story.
mbm-1769.quote: We read in our tent by lantern. When a moth settled on a page, my nephew decided it wanted that story. It picked three chapters of railway timetables. We gave them our best voices.

mbm-1770.clue: I made our missing glove into a pair.
mbm-1770.quote: There was a single felt glove in every kitchen drawer after our winter break. I traced them all for a quilt and turned the patterns over to give each its missing mate. We're still looking for their real mates.

mbm-1771.clue: Sometimes I sketch the waiting bench first.
mbm-1771.quote: At the little station a groove in the old bench fits my grandfather's walking stick. I sketched it before the train came in. He wanted two copies, one for each of his walking friends.

mbm-1772.clue: I keep the border unfinished till the doorbell rings.
mbm-1772.quote: Each visitor picks a scrap from my basket and adds one straight stitch to the border. My shyest cousin chose bright orange and stayed for a second stitch.

mbm-1773.clue: The popcorn trick works better cold.
mbm-1773.quote: I tried to pull a kernel from my neighbor's ear and a whole paper bag slipped off my knee. My audience liked the avalanche better. Now I save one kernel and bow to the clean-up crew.

mbm-1774.clue: I trust my partner with the soup when the music starts.
mbm-1774.quote: We took turns carrying lunch through a crowded hall between practices. When the music came back on she waltzed all the way to our table with a bowl in each hand. Not a drop.

mbm-1775.clue: I built the rescue robot for my smallest crew.
mbm-1775.quote: My niece's toy mice were always stuck in her cardboard lift. I made a mecha with a bright fold-down ramp. She tested it with four mice and one biscuit for the driver.
